title: Illinois: prepare financial-assurance options without assuming one is mandatory
description: Illinois publishes franchise filing, escrow, guaranty, surety-bond and deposit forms. Choose documents from the actual requirement and review.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The official form set tells you what to prepare
paragraphs: The Illinois Attorney General’s Franchise Bureau administers franchise registration and publishes the application, costs/source-of-funds, seller, consent-to-service, guaranty and accountant-consent forms. The same page includes escrow, surety-bond and deposit documents. Their availability is evidence of published processes, not evidence that every applicant must use every form.

sections.heading: Separate financial capacity from form completion
paragraphs: An overseas CFO should identify the selling entity’s own commitments and resources, any proposed guarantor and which entity will pay training and opening support costs. The team then matches requested assurance to actual documents and the cash model. The website does not approve a guarantor or predict an examiner’s decision.

sections.heading: Fictional example: initial support funded by the parent
paragraphs: A Swedish service brand expects its parent to fund training while a U.S. subsidiary signs franchises. The company secretary should not merely attach the parent’s accounts. Prepare an ownership chart, support-cost schedule, proposed commitment and correct statement/consent references so the filing reviewer can assess the chosen structure.

sections.heading: Useful preparation checklist
bullets: Current proposed FDD and agreements for the exact selling entity.
Initial obligations, timing and source-of-funds schedule.
Auditor consent referring to the correct financial statements.
Actual requested assurance and supporting agreement/form.
Separate review of offer timing, exemptions, advertising, relationship and broker duties.

sections.heading: Give the annual filing its own dated preparation record
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s currently linked annual tips sheet states a renewal due date 120 days after fiscal year end and describes matching issuance dates across the cover, certification, accountant consent and receipts. It calls for clean and blackline FDDs and the relevant forms, with revised B/C where changes occurred. It also describes requesting removal of financial assurance in the filing correspondence; that is a request for consideration, not automatic release.

The same undated sheet uses hardcopy/flash-drive/no-email instructions. Confirm the current accepted channel and fee before submission; this guide does not treat those format statements as proof that a particular 2026 filing will be accepted. Initial-sale timing, exemptions and operative statutory relationship protections remain separate open branches.

sections.heading: Coverage limit
paragraphs: The current statutory initial timing, fee and exemption tests have not been fully source-verified in this batch. They remain open requirements in the matrix. This preparation guide is not a statement that a filing is complete or an offering may start.

practicalOutput: An Illinois finance-and-document preparation package with open statutory questions recorded.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: Indiana: registration by notification still comes before covered offers
description: Indiana calls its franchise registration a notice filing process without merit review; exemption facts and annual dates still matter.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Apply the actual Indiana model described by the agency
paragraphs: The Securities Division’s current guidance quotes the Indiana franchise definition: a business right under a marketing plan/system prescribed in substantial part, substantial association with the designated commercial symbol, and a required franchise fee. Record the actual operating requirements, brand use and all payment flows, rather than assume a licence label or a single local operator resolves classification. Fee exclusions and a particular exemption still require their own facts.

sections.heading: Understand what the filing establishes
paragraphs: Indiana’s Securities Division says a franchisor must register before offering or selling unless exempt. It describes initial effectiveness on receipt if no stop order is in effect, a one-year period and a notice filing process without merit review. A filing receipt therefore does not substantiate commercial promises or certify the franchise.

sections.heading: The exemption is state-specific
paragraphs: The agency describes de minimis, large-net-worth, franchisee-sale and rule/order routes and says the burden of establishing an exemption rests with the claimant. It calls the described exemptions self-executing and offers an optional determination-letter procedure. Do not import a federal or another state’s exemption test.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Danish industrial-service pilot
paragraphs: A group investigates one Indiana operator and assumes that “one licence” is universally exempt. The correct preparation is to identify the specific Indiana route, sales history, related transactions and all conditions. The federal franchise rule and any relevant other states are analysed separately. A narrow state exemption is not one free franchise in every jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Build a filing-and-renewal owner
paragraphs: The agency lists a $500 initial fee, current FDD, seller disclosures, consent to service and supplemental materials. It says renewal must be filed no later than expiry; a lapse requires an initial filing and fee. The company secretary should retain exact filing/expiry dates and reconcile the entity and document versions.

sections.heading: An effective annual filing does not absorb every change
paragraphs: The current guidance requires an amended FDD within 30 days of a material change. Before providing a new FDD to prospects, the franchisor must file it as an updated FDD to the effective registration or submit an explicitly requested early renewal. Record the change date, affected documents, filing and intended delivery. Do not wait for ordinary annual expiry to review a material change.

The agency’s statute links use a 2024 code path; the attempted current legislature PDF route returned an application shell, not operative code. These are the agency’s actual current instructions, not a claim that the full current Indiana relationship statute has been read.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
bullets: Precise transaction and exemption applicability.
Independent disclosure timing and agreement changes.
Advertising and ongoing relationship rules.
Operating licences, customer bid conditions and local premises requirements.

practicalOutput: An Indiana registration-or-exemption record with an annual renewal owner.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: Michigan: annual notice filing and disclosure use different clocks
description: Michigan’s notice-only process does not remove state disclosure requirements or turn an FDD into an approved document.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The agency’s definition is a separate state screen
paragraphs: Michigan’s current Attorney General page quotes a three-element definition: a substantially prescribed marketing plan/system, substantial association with the designated commercial symbol and a direct or indirect required franchise fee. It covers express/implied and oral/written arrangements. Record those facts and separately investigate actual fee exclusions or other scope issues. The federal result and the word licence do not automatically decide Michigan classification.

sections.heading: File the notice before the covered activity
paragraphs: MCL 445.1507a requires an annual notice before offering or selling in the state. The agency describes a Notice of Intent, a $250 fee and annual repetition. It also says it does not review FDD compliance. Filing is evidence of a notice; it is not a legal opinion on the documents.

sections.heading: Count business days separately
paragraphs: MCL 445.1508 requires disclosure, the prescribed Michigan notice and proposed agreements at least ten business days before binding agreement or consideration, whichever occurs first. The federal 14-calendar-day disclosure requirement is independent. The team should satisfy both applicable clocks, accounting for the actual dates, rather than converting ten business days into a fixed calendar-day count.

sections.heading: The state notice is substantive
paragraphs: Section 8 describes a Michigan disclosure page and prohibited-term notice. It says the existence of a notice on file does not constitute approval, recommendation or endorsement. Record the correct state page and the agreement version delivered; do not reduce the task to sending a generic home-market brochure.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Thai training business
paragraphs: A manager plans to accept a partner deposit after a long holiday weekend. The company secretary records the delivery date and separately calculates federal calendar days and Michigan business days for the planned payment and signature events. If any assumption about delivery or holiday treatment is unresolved, the date remains pending.

sections.heading: Evidence to retain
bullets: Filed annual notice and its anniversary.
Delivered FDD, Michigan page and all proposed agreements.
Recipient and delivery evidence.
Independent calendar and business-day calculations.
Changes to the proposed agreement and who initiated them.

practicalOutput: A Michigan notice record and dual-clock disclosure schedule.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: Minnesota: registration and financial assurance are different tasks
description: Minnesota’s financial-assurance guidance explains why an initial franchise fee may be unavailable to fund immediate support.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Apply Minnesota’s own definition and alternative branches
paragraphs: Current 80C.01 subdivision 4 includes the brand/right, community-of-interest and direct/indirect fee arrangement, but also other branches concerning fuel, specified business-opportunity promises and certain security-system payments. Area-franchise and fee definitions and all exclusions require their own review. It is not sufficient to substitute the federal control/assistance test or inspect only the contract title.

Build a model/fee/support factsheet: required initial and recurring payments, goods/services/training, rights granted, brand use, shared marketing interest and any claimed wholesale/fair-market-value exclusion. This source identifies the screen; it does not decide that an actual arrangement is covered or exempt.

sections.heading: Registration comes before covered offers and sales
paragraphs: Minnesota Statutes 80C.02 requires an effective registration before a covered offer or sale unless the franchise or transaction is exempt under 80C.03. The Department’s page directs electronic filings through ComOnline and describes a 12-month registration period from the commissioner’s order.

sections.heading: Do not fund support with inaccessible fees
paragraphs: The financial-assurance guidance says the commissioner may require escrow, impoundment or deferral where adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated. It describes a surety-bond alternative and deferral of initial franchise fees until the franchisee has opened. A requested condition is part of the cash model; it is not proof that every applicant faces the same restriction.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a German maintenance brand
paragraphs: The support office expects to pay a trainer and travel costs from an initial fee received at signature. If the applicable condition defers that fee until the operator opens, the support office needs another funding source during the intervening period. The CFO should model the dated receipts and payments under the actual condition rather than just recognising fee revenue.

sections.heading: Prepare before the financial review
bullets: Map each initial support obligation and when its cost is paid.
Identify committed capital that is available before any deferred or impounded fee release.
Keep the selected financial condition, agreement terms and release evidence.
Assign financial statements, filing forms and renewal dates to the company secretary and CFO.

sections.heading: Maintain the registration and the relationship separately
paragraphs: Section 80C.08 makes the registration effective for 12 months from the commissioner’s order and requires the annual report before that period ends. Record the order and actual end date. An annual registration task is different from a contract renewal with an existing franchisee. The separate Minnesota relationship guide addresses 80C.14’s termination, nonrenewal and transfer branches; a filing renewal does not itself approve those actions.

sections.heading: Two disclosure requirements, plus a retained receipt
paragraphs: The seven-day language on the agency page matches current 2026 Minnesota Statutes 80C.06 subdivision 5. For a franchise subject to state registration requirements, it calls for the current public offering statement and all proposed agreements at least seven days before the earlier of any franchise or other agreement or consideration. A signed acknowledgement must be obtained before agreement/payment and retained three years.

The federal 14-calendar-day disclosure requirement remains independent where applicable. The state seven-day rule does not shorten it. Keep the documents, triggers and dates separate rather than choosing whichever interval is shorter.

practicalOutput: A Minnesota support-funding schedule that treats any financial-assurance condition explicitly.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: Maryland: an exemption can preserve disclosure and notice duties
description: Maryland registration exemptions have their own conditions; specified routes preserve earlier disclosure events.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Check the defined model and fee first
paragraphs: Section 14-201 uses an express/implied, oral/written agreement with a substantially prescribed marketing plan/system, substantial commercial-symbol association and a direct/indirect franchise fee. Area franchises are included. The fee definition includes goods/services payments but lists specific exclusions, including specified wholesale, fair-market-value and other arrangements. Map the actual payments and rights before choosing a registration or exemption route.

sections.heading: Begin with the actual offer
paragraphs: Business Regulation 14-214 requires registration before a covered offer, including advertising, or sale, subject to stated exceptions. COMAR 02.02.08.10 then supplies particular exemption routes. An exemption from registration is not a universal exemption from the rest of the franchise law.

sections.heading: Identify the selected exemption and its clock
paragraphs: For specified exemptions in paragraphs D–G, COMAR states that absent a contrary order the offering circular and agreements must be delivered at the earlier of the first personal meeting or ten business days before signing or payment. Specified routes also have notice conditions. This first-meeting trigger shows why a universal “we can disclose fourteen days before payment” rule is inadequate.

sections.heading: Reconcile the source versions
paragraphs: The regulation uses legacy UFOC terminology and references alongside current franchise practice. The task is to reconcile the applicable statute, regulation and current agency instructions for the selected exemption. This page records the rule’s explicit language and leaves transaction-specific application conditional; it does not silently discard the earlier trigger.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Belgian technical-services group
paragraphs: The team assumes a large-company exemption permits an immediate in-person recruitment meeting. Its launch planner instead records the proposed meeting, buyer facts, selected exemption and disclosure/notice prerequisites. A responsible reviewer confirms the route and timing before the relevant commitment.

sections.heading: Use the actual effectiveness, renewal and amendment conditions
paragraphs: Under 14-218, absent a stop order, registration automatically takes effect at noon on the 30th business day after the application or last amendment is filed, or an earlier time the Commissioner sets. A receipt and an effective registration are different events. Section 14-219 normally uses the first anniversary and requires renewal materials at least 15 business days before expiration, subject to its order/other conditions.

Section 14-220 requires a prompt material-change amendment and, if approved, an effective date set by the Commissioner. Do not invent a fixed 30-day amendment period or wait until annual renewal. Preserve the change, submission, order and document-delivery dates separately.

sections.heading: Keep the sale-conditioned waiver restriction narrow
paragraphs: Section 14-226 bars requiring a prospective franchisee, as a condition of sale, to agree to a release, assignment, novation, waiver or estoppel relieving a person from liability under the subtitle. Flag the actual contract and any questionnaires or side papers for that review. This provision does not itself decide every later dispute settlement, termination condition or choice-of-law question.

sections.heading: Advertising stays on the work list
paragraphs: COMAR .09 calls for a copy of covered advertising at least five days before anticipated initial use. Maintain an inventory of the material, exact version, sponsor, channel and first-use date. Keep advertising review separate from the exemption evidence.

practicalOutput: A Maryland exemption checklist with first-meeting, notice and advertising dates.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: New York: separate sale meetings, material changes and annual renewal
description: New York’s current registration guide ties annual renewal submissions to 120 days after fiscal year end and gives advertising its own lead time.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the state’s actual model and sales facts
paragraphs: The Attorney General currently says offerings must be registered before franchises are offered or sold in or from New York unless an exemption applies. Part 200.1 supplies specific fee and marketing-plan meanings: payments can take different forms and advice/training can include operational, technical, financial and promotional assistance. Collect the actual payments, rights and support, not just the word licence.

The complete current General Business Law 681 statutory definition was not retrieved because its official route returned 403. These regulatory inputs are a useful classification factsheet, not a replacement for that whole statutory test or an exemption determination.

sections.heading: Use the company’s fiscal calendar
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s guide directs renewal submissions annually within 120 days after the franchisor’s fiscal year end. It distinguishes a timely pending renewal from an expired registration. If registration expires, the guide says no covered offers or sales within or from New York until the renewal is submitted and accepted for filing.

sections.heading: The renewal is a management reporting task
paragraphs: The guide asks for the updated FDD, changes marked against the registered version, accountant consent and annual information about franchise sales, prices, credit terms and audited financial statements. Finance and sales operations both hold needed evidence. Start with an accountable owner and internal preparation dates, not a reminder on the last permissible day.

sections.heading: Advertising has a separate schedule
paragraphs: The same guide calls for two copies of franchise advertising through NASAA FRED at least seven days before intended use. A timely renewal submission does not itself establish that the new recruitment campaign has met its advertising task.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a UK training network
paragraphs: The franchisor’s fiscal year ends before the commercial team’s busiest recruitment period. The CFO records the year-end renewal deadline; the expansion director separately records campaign publication and advertising-submission dates. If the registration lapses, the team records the affected activity and the conditions for resuming it rather than assuming the website can continue selling.

sections.heading: A meeting can be earlier than the planned signature
paragraphs: The currently linked state addendum, internally revised April 2, 2024, says the FDD must be delivered at the earliest of the first personal meeting or ten business days before execution of the franchise/other agreement or payment of related consideration. Preserve that literal agency text alongside the independent federal 14-calendar-day rule. Do not schedule every transaction only by counting 14 days backward from signature.

The addendum references GBL 683(8); the direct current statute body was access-blocked in this review. The quoted agency requirement is retained openly, rather than silently rewritten or treated as a completed transaction-specific reconciliation. Record meeting, delivery, agreement and payment facts before relying on a date.

sections.heading: A material change is not just an annual-report item
paragraphs: Part 200.5 requires prompt notification by application to amend for material prospectus changes. Its examples include fees and specified significant adverse business, obligation, agreement and product/model changes, as well as the stated financial information. Keep a change register and affected versions independently of the 120-day annual process. Current filing guidance controls the submission channel.

sections.heading: Do not let side papers erase the preserved-rights review
paragraphs: The current addendum addresses preservation of applicable statutory rights for renewal/transfer and choice clauses, and says commencement questionnaires/acknowledgments cannot have the stated claim-waiver or reliance-disclaimer effect. Compare the whole signing package with the actual addendum and applicable law. These provisions are not an automatic ruling on every negotiated dispute or every future termination.

sections.heading: Output for the board pack
bullets: Fiscal year-end date and calculated review deadline.
Named owner for audited statements and sales/credit information.
Registered and proposed FDD versions with change log.
Advertising inventory, submitted versions and intended-use dates.

practicalOutput: A fiscal-year-based renewal checklist and a separate advertising register.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: North Dakota: update renewal timing and remove outdated addendum assumptions
description: North Dakota’s current agency page gives a pre-expiry renewal deadline and a specific April 2026 change to its FDD addendum practice.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Classify the agreement and the state-connected offer
paragraphs: Section 51-19-02 covers the stated marketing-plan/system, commercial-symbol and direct/indirect fee combination, including area-franchise scope. Required goods/services can matter, while the wholesale-goods exclusion has a reasonable-quantity condition. The same section defines state-connected offers/acceptances and distinguishes uninterrupted renewals/extensions in its offer/sale definition. That contract-renewal qualification does not cancel registration-renewal duties.

sections.heading: A filed application is not the final effectiveness event
paragraphs: Section 51-19-03 requires registration or an applicable exemption before a covered offer/sale. Under 51-19-07, no stop order plus filing and entry by the Commissioner into the register are relevant to effectiveness. Material changes require prompt written amendment notification; approved amendments take effect on the Commissioner’s date. Conditional fee escrow/impoundment or a surety alternative also has its own statutory/actual-order facts.

sections.heading: Set the renewal work before the expiry date
paragraphs: The agency directs renewal no later than fifteen business days before registration expires unless the commissioner waives the period. It describes a twelve-month registration period unless an order or rule says otherwise. A same-day expiry reminder does not provide the required preparation window.

sections.heading: A changed form requirement is not deregulation
paragraphs: The page expressly states that from April 1, 2026 a state-specific FDD addendum is no longer required. This is a narrow document change. The registration, financial review, disclosure and amendment tasks do not disappear. A source change should flag dependent pages and templates for editorial review rather than automatically rewriting every obligation.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Netherlands maintenance network
paragraphs: The team reuses last year’s filing checklist. The coordinator finds the agency’s dated addendum notice, marks that template item for revision and preserves the reviewed prior version. The renewal owner separately checks the FDD, changes marked against the prior version, accountant consent, seller forms and advertising not previously filed.

sections.heading: Assign the evidence
bullets: Effective registration and expiry dates from the actual record.
Business-day renewal deadline with any written waiver.
Current filing instructions and a reviewed checklist revision.
Financial-assurance condition if applicable.
Material-change reporting owner and document-version log.

sections.heading: Keep disclosure, receipts and contract rights separate
paragraphs: Section 51-19-08(6) has its stated seven-day prospectus/agreement delivery rule before the earlier agreement or consideration, a signed receipt and three-year receipt retention. The applicable federal 14-calendar-day rule remains independent; the state text does not shorten it. Section 51-19-16(7) separately makes purported waiver of compliance with the chapter/rules/orders void. This is a named anti-waiver provision, not a full decision on all termination, renewal or sector protections.

sections.heading: Do not repeat the agency’s national state count
paragraphs: The source contains a broad count of registration states. This site does not reuse it as a national legal classification. Notice filing, merit review, exemptions and relationship laws are recorded independently for each jurisdiction.

practicalOutput: A current North Dakota renewal checklist and traceable April 2026 template revision.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: Minnesota franchise changes: termination and nonrenewal use different tests
description: Prepare cause, notice/cure, expiry and transfer evidence under 80C.14 rather than treating every exit as the same event.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review
limitations: 80C.14 within its franchise/classification scope only; no actual termination, nonrenewal or transfer approved.
No going-concern valuation or complete commissioner-rule, sector, bankruptcy or judicial analysis.

sections.heading: Define the relationship and the action
paragraphs: First apply 80C.01 and the recognized-classification context in 80C.14 subdivisions 1–2. Then describe whether the proposed action is termination/cancellation, failure to renew, or withholding consent to a transfer. Registration expiry and contract expiry are different events. A calendar label cannot substitute for the actual conduct.

sections.heading: Keep cause apart from the notice exception
paragraphs: Subdivision 3 requires good cause and states a 90-day written notice with all reasons and 60 days from receipt to correct, subject to its separate immediate-effect exceptions. Those exceptions concern specified abandonment, business-related conviction and the prescribed uncured goodwill-default branch. Do not assume every fact in the good-cause list also appears in the immediate-notice list.

Preserve the material/reasonable requirement, what failed, notice contents, actual receipt and correction. The source’s goodwill branch itself requires the prescribed prior cure notice. A clause saying breach permits immediate exit does not establish the statutory facts.

sections.heading: Nonrenewal is not simply termination at expiry
paragraphs: Subdivision 4 separately addresses good-cause/failure-to-correct cases and the route requiring at least 180 days’ advance notice plus the stated opportunity to operate long enough to recover fair market value as a going concern, measured from the failure to renew. Do not replace that language with a guaranteed cash refund or simple initial-fee calculation.

It also prohibits refusing renewal for the purpose of converting the franchisee’s premises to the franchisor’s own operation. Identify the real plan and evidence rather than selecting the word nonrenewal because the term is ending.

sections.heading: A transfer request has another question
paragraphs: Subdivision 5 addresses unreasonably withholding consent where the replacement meets the franchisor’s present qualifications and standards. Keep the proposed buyer’s evidence, current standards and actual reasons for a decision. This is not a declaration that every transfer must be approved.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: expiry during a performance dispute
paragraphs: Fictional example: a service brand plans not to renew an operator after weak results and wants to run the same premises itself. Management records the actual purpose, requirements, cure history and renewal facts before issuing a letter. The exercise does not decide good cause, value or a lawful outcome.

sections.heading: Prepare the action matrix
bullets: Define the covered relationship and applicable classification/rules.
Identify actual conduct: early termination, expiry/nonrenewal or transfer.
Separate good-cause facts from the notice exception relied on.
Record every notice, receipt, cure step and relevant expiry date.
For nonrenewal, preserve the actual purpose and going-concern-operation evidence.
For transfer, retain qualifications, current standards and reasons; obtain an actual decision on the facts.

title: Registration versus notice: compare the actual trigger and legal effect
description: Use Michigan, Indiana, Maryland and North Dakota to separate filing labels, effectiveness, document review and disclosure clocks.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review
limitations: Only the named current statutory/agency distinctions; not an all-state classification or national count.
Actual franchise status, state nexus, exemptions, complete filing/stop-order facts and other states remain separate.

sections.heading: The label is not the permission
paragraphs: A management team needs the applicable legal event, not a colour on a national map. Record whether a filing is required before a covered offer, what makes it effective, whether a stop order changes the result and which renewal/amendment duties continue. Keep franchise definition, state nexus and exemption evidence ahead of that analysis.

sections.heading: Four current examples show different mechanisms
paragraphs: These are selected examples, not a ranking of jurisdictions or a claim that every registration has the same review.

headers: What the filing does not prove
rows: Annual Notice of Intent under 445.1507a/AG guidance
Required before covered offers/sales; repeat annually
AG says it does not review FDD compliance and does not endorse the offering
Registration by notification under current Division guidance
Initial effectiveness on receipt if no stop order; one-year registration
Agency expressly says no review of offering merits; registration is not a finding documents are true/complete
Absent stop order, noon on 30th business day after application or last amendment, or earlier Commissioner-set time
A receipt alone is not that effectiveness event or a complete exemption determination
Filing plus Commissioner’s entry in register, with no stop order; amendments have their own effective date
51-19-11 prohibits portraying filing/registration as a merits or document-truth finding

sections.heading: A notice state can still have disclosure and contract rules
paragraphs: Michigan’s notice filing does not replace its separate ten-business-day disclosure package under 445.1508. Indiana’s current page separately requires material-change filing within 30 days and updated-FDD filing before delivery as described. Maryland and North Dakota have their own continuing amendment/renewal conditions. None of those labels changes the independent federal 14-calendar-day disclosure rule where it applies.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: four submissions on one day
paragraphs: Fictional example: an overseas brand’s U.S. entity submits paperwork for four proposed markets on the same day and wants one campaign start date. The coordinator records each applicable definition/nexus/exemption, the actual filing and effectiveness evidence, and separate document/meeting/payment clocks. A single upload date cannot supply all four states’ prerequisites. No actual filing or sale is approved by the example.

sections.heading: Build the ledger around events
bullets: Identify the actual franchisor, offer origins/destinations, buyer and operating facts.
Record the selected definition/exemption analysis and exact source.
Keep application/notice receipt separate from effectiveness, register entry and any order.
Track the applicable FDD/agreement delivery, meetings, signature and consideration dates separately.
Assign annual expiry, material-change and advertising tasks to named owners.
Treat examiner correspondence or a filing receipt as evidence of its actual event, not certification of profitability or legal compliance.
